```plato

    //==
    // # Evaluation of the declared polynomial types
    //
    // The array-backed forms fold their coefficient arrays with the P2 `Reduce`
    // primitive. Power-basis polynomials (dense, sparse, power series) evaluate
    // by Horner's rule below. The classical-basis series (Chebyshev, Legendre,
    // Hermite, Bernstein, Fourier) still await basis-specific recurrences
    // (Clenshaw / de Casteljau) rather than plain Horner; those are also
    // foldable but out of scope for this pass.

    // Evaluates a dense coefficient array given in ASCENDING powers at x by
    // Horner's rule (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horner%27s_method): folding
    // the highest-power coefficient first means no explicit power of x is ever
    // formed, which is both faster and more stable.
    // An empty array is the zero polynomial and evaluates to 0.
    HornerEval(coefficients: Array<Number>, x: Number): Number
        => MapRange(coefficients.Count, i => coefficients[coefficients.Count - 1 - i])
               .Reduce(0.0, (acc, c) => acc * x + c);
```
